Recap of Part 1

Part 1 built the core loop. The agent hears a voice note or sees the screen, asks Gemma 4, and acts through checked tools.

Part 1: the map of the core loop

Part 1: one chat turn through brain.respond()

agent/brain.py respond()
query = " ".join(p["text"] for p in user if p["type"] == "text")
names = select_tools(query, history or [])
system = system_prompt() + (SPOKEN if spoken else "") + _waiting_calls()
hits = _recall(query, use_memory)
lines = [f"({m['when']}, {m['kind']}) {m['text']}" for m in hits]
msgs, used = fit_budget(system, lines, history or [], user, tools.schemas(names))
...
for step in range(max_steps):
...
params = {"chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": True}} if step > 0 else {}
msg = send(msgs, tools=tools.schemas(names), **params)["choices"][0]["message"]
if calls := msg.get("tool_calls") or []:
    msgs.append({"role": "assistant", "content": msg.get("content") or "", "tool_calls": calls})
    retries_left = _handle_calls(calls, msgs, trace, retries_left)
    text = _fixed_reply(trace, retries_left)
else:
    text = _final_text(msg.get("content") or "", trace, msgs)
if text is not None:
    return {"text": text, **out}
  1. 1Offer 5 toolsselect_tools() compares the request and your last 3 messages with an embedding of each tool. Gemma gets the 5 closest. No tool runs yet.
  2. 2Add 3 memoriesThe 3 closest memories go into the system prompt, with their time and kind.
  3. 3Fit the budgetRemove the oldest history, then memories, until it fits: 16,384 tokens, minus 1,024 for the reply.
  4. 4Send to GemmaOne local HTTP request goes to llama-server. Gemma replies with text or with tool calls.
  5. 5Run the calls, or check the textcheck() runs first, and the results go back to Gemma. A call that waits for approval ends the turn. A claim with no call gets one retry.
  6. How we measure it
    Input
    16 synthetic requests.
    Output
    The tool call that Gemma makes.
    Metrics
    Exact tool calls 1.0 (limit 0.80). The right tool is in the 5 offered: 1.0.

Part 1: the model never decides permissions

agent/tools/__init__.py check()
if name not in REGISTRY:
    return "invalid", f"unknown tool '{name}'"
t = REGISTRY[name]
try:
    jsonschema.validate(args, t.parameters)
except jsonschema.ValidationError as e:
    return "invalid", f"bad arguments: {e.message}"
if t.tier == BLOCKED:
    return "blocked", f"'{name}' is in the blocked tier"
if t.guard and (reason := t.guard(args)):
    return "blocked", reason
if t.tier == CONFIRM:
    return "confirm", f"'{name}' needs your approval"
return "ok", ""
  • Safe: 6 toolsget_time, calculator, save_note, search_memory, list_files and read_file run at once.
  • Confirm: 2 toolswrite_file and run_shell wait. You approve or deny the call in the dashboard.
  • Blocked: 1 tooldelete_file never runs, whatever the model asks.
  • GuardsA guard stops one unsafe call. The path guard stops secrets files. The shell guard stops dangerous commands.
  • Pending is not doneThe model once said “I have created the file” while write_file still waited. Now code writes that reply.

Each tool is one entry in the tool registry, with a JSON schema and a tier. Of 28 synthetic calls, 16 were unsafe. None of the 16 ran.

Part 1: senses, tasks, memory, evals, plug-ins

  • Hearsenses/audio.pyThe Silero VAD finds speech. A pause under 0.6 s does not end it. chunk() cuts clips under 28 s, because llama.cpp splits audio over 30 s.
  • Seesenses/screen.py, video.pyA screenshot shrinks to 1280 pixels on its longest side: about 400 tokens. A screen video is at most 60 s, sent at 1 frame per second.
  • Tasks 1 and 2brain.ask_json()llama.cpp turns the JSON schema into a grammar. Code checks the reply again, with one retry. A voice note gives action items, a screenshot a fix.
  • Memorymemory/episodic.pyJunk and near copies are not stored. EmbeddingGemma-2 gives each memory a vector of 768 numbers. Each chat turn gets the 3 closest memories.
  • Evalsevals/<component>/eval.pyEach eval has load_cases(), run_item() and score(). config.THRESHOLDS holds the limit of each metric.
  • Plug-insplatforms/, accel/Code that differs by OS or GPU lives in one plug-in file. Core code calls platforms.current(). Only macOS and Metal are verified.

Multimodal Personal Agent

Recap of Part 2

Part 2 made the agent run all day as its own process. It hears when you let it, keeps what matters, and learns from your feedback.

Part 2: two processes share one set of files

  • events.emit(kind, ...)Each component writes one row to the event log: a dotted kind such as senses.audio, the source process and a JSON payload.
  • events.since(id)A reader asks for the rows after the last id that it saw. A kind prefix can filter them.
  • A kill -9 of the daemonThe dashboard stays up. The next daemon (the login item, or Start in the dashboard) reads the same files and continues.

Part 2: the daemon runs one job at a time, in steps

agent/daemon.py Daemon.tick()
for _name, kind, reason in due():
    checkpoint.submit(kind, {}, reason)
if self.models:
    for kind, args, reason in triggers():
        checkpoint.submit(kind, args, reason)
self._sync_listener()
j = checkpoint.claim_next()
if j and j["kind"] in JOBS:
    self.run_job(j)
elif j:
    checkpoint.finish(j["id"], "failed", f"unknown job kind '{j['kind']}'")
agent/checkpoint.py step()
done, value = stored_result(job_id, name)
if done:
    events.emit("checkpoint.skipped", job_id=job_id, step=name)
    return value
_record(job_id, name, "intent", intent or {})
_record(job_id, name, "execution", {})
value = fn()
_record(job_id, name, "result", value)
return value
  1. 1The scheduleOnce a second, the daemon checks the clock with due(). It queues a job only when a slot of config.SCHEDULE arrives (summaries every 15 minutes, the brief at 18:00). After a sleep, only the newest missed slot runs.
  2. 2Triggers20 new transcripts queue a summary when a window closes.
  3. 3One jobThe oldest queued job runs: from the schedule, a trigger or the dashboard.
  4. 4Skip what finishedA step with a stored result returns it. Its code does not run again.
  5. 5Intent, run, resultTwo rows go to SQLite before the code runs. Only the result row marks it as finished.
  6. How we measure it
    Input
    3 jobs, each killed with kill -9 during a step.
    Output
    Steps that run again, and the time to the next step.
    Metrics
    0 steps redone, 0 jobs lost. 0.11 s to the next step (limit 10 s).

Part 2: the agent hears, remembers and learns

  • Listen when you let itambient.py SegmenterThe daemon listens only while you turn it on. The Segmenter ends an utterance after 0.6 s of silence, or at 28 s.
  • Whisper writes the textsenses/stt.pyWhisper large-v3-turbo keeps Gemma 4 free for you. Each utterance becomes one raw transcript row, with a text and an audio vector.
  • Summaries cite their rowsmemory/consolidate.pyEvery 15 minutes, each closed window of 30 minutes becomes a summary and facts. The schema allows only the ids of that window.
  • Forget and searchforget(), episodic.search()Raw rows that a summary covers are deleted after 7 days. Screenshots and clips also get a vector, so a search can use them.
  • Task 3: recalltasks.recall()“What did we decide this morning?” searches 05:00 to 12:00. The top 6 memories go in, and the answer names their ids.
  • Task 4: learnagent/evolve.pyYour feedback on the daily brief becomes a patch. Code allows only style and preference changes, then tests them on 3 other days.

8 of 8Task 3 questions answered right, with memory ids

Parts 1 and 2: six rules to keep in mind

  • The model never decides permissionstools.check()Each tool call passes the schema, the tier and the guard. A confirm tool waits for you.
  • The model proposes, code decidesask_json(), validate_patch()Code checks each JSON reply, each cited id and each prompt patch before it stores anything.
  • A step is safe to run twicecheckpoint.step()A crash can repeat one step. Stored results, window keys and the duplicate filter make that safe.
  • Processes share filesdata/runtime/*.sqliteThe daemon and the dashboard share only SQLite files and the event log. One continues when the other stops.
  • One file for each machineplatforms/, accel/Code that differs by OS or GPU lives in one plug-in file. Core code calls it.
  • A number and a limitevals/, config.THRESHOLDSEach part has an eval. The cases are synthetic, so add your own before you trust a score.

Multimodal Personal Agent

Voice, native skills, MCP connectors

Now the agent speaks, wakes on its name, speaks up on its own, and uses tools from other programs.

The goal: an agent that you talk to

Part 2 runs all day, but it writes only text, and it uses only the tools in its own code. Part 3 gives it a voice, and other programs can add tools.

  • It speaksagent/voice/tts.py, speaker.pyKokoro-82M turns each sentence into audio on the CPU. The dashboard tab plays it.
  • It wakes on its nameagent/voice/wake.pyA pretrained openWakeWord model. On a low score, Whisper listens for “Jarvis”.
  • You can stop itagent/voice/turn.pySay the wake word while it speaks, or press Stop. A follow-up needs no name.
  • It speaks upagent/proactive.pyA failed test on your screen or a due reminder becomes speech, a notification and a feed row.
  • Native skillsagent/skills/A folder with a manifest and one Python file becomes a tool.
  • MCP connectorsagent/mcp_client.pyPaste a standard mcpServers config. Each MCP server shows as on-device or remote.

“Hey Jarvis, remind me to call Mike in two minutes.” Two minutes later, the agent says it.

One spoken reminder, from the name to the voice

Wakewake.py“Hey Jarvis” ends. A score of 0.5 or more wakes it at once. A lower score waits for Whisper to hear “Jarvis” (about 1.2 s).
→
Recordturn.pyThe request ends after 0.6 s of silence.
→
Transcribesenses/stt.pyWhisper writes the text in about 0.9 s.
→
Replybrain.pyGemma calls reminders__add_reminder on the MCP server.
→
Speakspeaker.pyKokoro turns the first sentence into audio in about 0.4 s. The dashboard tab plays it.
→
2 min laterproactive.pyThe daemon checks for due reminders every 15 s. The agent says it.
  • At any time: stop itturn.py, voice.jsSay “Hey Jarvis” or press S. The dashboard tab stops the audio in about 62 ms.
  • All the time: the screenproactive.pyTask 5 looks at the screen every 5 s. A failed test that stays on screen is said only once in 5 minutes.

Our target for one spoken turn is 4.85 s (LATENCY_BUDGET). A measured turn takes 7.5 to 9 s, because the reply after a tool call needs thinking on: without it, Gemma 4 sends back an empty reply.

    self.mels = np.vstack((self.mels, self._mel(np.concatenate((self.context, frame)))))[-10 * 97 :]
...

    if score >= self.threshold:
    return self._wake(frame)

if maybe and self.check_at is None and frame > self.no_check_until:
...

    1. 1Two frozen models_mel() and _embedding() each run one ONNX model: 80 ms of audio become a mel spectrogram, then 96 numbers. Their weights never change, and every wake word uses them.
    2. 2The pretrained classifierThe last 16 embeddings (1.28 s) give a score from 0 to 1. This classifier (1.3 MB) is openWakeWord's “hey jarvis”.
    3. 3Sure or maybe0.5 or more wakes at once. From 0.1, it is a “maybe”: Whisper reads the last 2 s and must hear “jarvis”.
    4. LessonOn my voice, the classifier alone woke 0 of 15 times (scores 0.12 to 0.49). With Whisper: 10 of 15, in about 1.2 s.

    Wake word: we trained one, then a pretrained one won

    Why it won
    • More and better clipsAbout 200,000 synthetic clips in many voices, with noise and rooms. We made 10,000 clips with one engine.
    • Same codeIt reads the same 16 embeddings. Only config.WAKE_MODEL changed. Our numpy steps match openWakeWord within 1.2e-6.
    
    
    What it costs
    • The name alone wakes it“Jarvis was the butler” scores 0.996.
    • Real voices score lowReal voices scored under 0.5: 0 of 15 woke. So we added the Whisper check of the slide before.
    
  
    
  
    A new name needs a new model, and a model is only as good as its clips. A pretrained name is cheaper.

    ready.set_result([_tool_info(t) for t in listing.tools])
      
    
      1. 1A server with a nameMCPServer is from the official Python SDK, mcp 2.3.0.
      2. 2A function becomes a toolOne line of description for the model. The SDK makes the JSON schema from the type hints. Annotations are only hints.
      3. 3Requests on stdinThe client starts this file as a process. mcp.run() reads requests on stdin and writes replies on stdout.
      4. 4The client lists the toolsOne session per server. The Tools tab shows its tools, and you enable each one.
      5. LessonMCPServer sends the whole docstring as the description, unless you give description=. One line is better for a small model.
      6. How we measure it
        Input
        6 synthetic spoken reminder requests.
        Output
        The stored reminder.
        Metrics
        6 of 6: the right words, due within 30 s of the time asked.

        agent/mcp_client.py  _register_tool()

    name=f"{server}{SEPARATOR}{name}",

        agent/mcp_client.py  Hub.call()
        queue = self.queues.get(server)
if queue is None or self.loop is None:
    raise RuntimeError(f"MCP server '{server}' is not connected")
reply: concurrent.futures.Future = concurrent.futures.Future()
self.loop.call_soon_threadsafe(queue.put_nowait, (tool, args, reply))
result = reply.result(timeout=config.MCP_CALL_TIMEOUT_S)
if result.is_error:
    raise RuntimeError(str(_text_of(result)))
return _text_of(result)
        
    
        1. 1A name and a labelThe tool is <server>__<tool>. Its description names the server and its label.
        2. 2Tier, then the callThe tier is your choice. The function only calls the hub, after tools.check().
        3. 3Queue it, then waitThe SDK is async, the brain is not. The call goes to the server's session in the event loop, and waits up to 60 s.
        4. LessonA stdio server gets only HOME, PATH and a few safe variables. A variable from the agent never reached it, so the server takes its file as --db.
        5. How we measure it
          Input
          20 requests, a catalog of 40 tools like common MCP servers.
          Output
          The tool that Gemma calls.
          Metrics
          85% with 5, 20 or 40 tools. Top 5 of 40 only: 80% (limit 80%).

        Four rules that explain Part 3
        
  
        • 1. The model reports, the code decidescheck_screen(), skills.check(), tools.check()Gemma lists the failed tests. Code decides to speak, and code checks each manifest, tier and secret.
        • 2. One registry for every tooltools.REGISTRYBuilt-in tools, skills and MCP tools all pass schema, tier and guard. A new MCP tool starts at confirm.
        • 3. Speech is eventsvoice.say, voice.chunk, voice.stopAny process can speak, and any process can stop it. The events also hold the times for the evals.
        • 4. The voice plays where people hear itdashboard/voice.py, play_audioThe tab plays it for Google Meet. Without a tab, this machine's speakers play it.
        
  
        Next, you see each rule in the code while it runs.
